name: email
doc: Checking that a receiver is who it says, by mail. A receiver is contacted when mail sent to its address is delivered, and verified when it answers for that address. A test of a receiver passes only when both hold, and each way of contacting or verifying a receiver is a proof of one of the two propositions. The mailboxes in the proofs are simulated: nothing here sends mail to a real address.

types.name: EmailReceiver
types.doc: Something that can be reached by email at an address, and the mailbox that answers for it.

fields.name: address
fields.doc: The address mail is sent to.

fields.name: provider
fields.doc: Which mailbox answers for the address. An inbox delivers to any address and answers for the ones it owns; a bounce delivers to none.

types.name: Verdict
types.doc: Whether a receiver passed a test, and if it did not, the first part that failed.

fields.name: reason
fields.doc: The first part that failed, absent when it passed.

functions.name: contacted
functions.doc: Whether mail sent to the receiver's address is delivered. A proof of this is one way of reaching a receiver.

functions.name: verified
functions.doc: Whether the receiver answers for its address, which shows it is who it says. A proof of this is one way of checking identity.

functions.name: test_email
functions.doc: The verifier: a receiver passes when it is contacted and then verified. The reasons are `not_contacted` and `not_verified`. Has no proofs of its own, since it is built from the two above.
